stages.prompt:
DO
Goal: the documentation this item's change affects says what the change now does.
Consult, and cite the headings you used:
- spec (## Requirements): the R-<n> this item changed, for the intended behaviour.
- architecture.md (## Structure, ## Interfaces and boundaries, ## Decisions): what is now true; a design or service decision this item made is an AD-<n> under ## Decisions (write it if implement did not).
- environment.md (## Commands): the commands your examples use.

INVOKE /until-loop NOW with the argument below, verbatim. Do this stage's work only inside that loop.
/until-loop
  Work (one iteration): Run each changed public behaviour (from the change inventory) and update the README, API, operator and error documentation from what you observe, including the errors a user can see and how to turn on diagnostics; state known limits and caveats; link to the authoritative home instead of copying a contract; then reread every document you changed and run its commands and examples.
  Exit when ALL of these hold (each shown by a command or file, after the last edit):
    1. Every changed public behaviour (each public entry point, command, API, setting or screen in <run>/lint/<id>-inventory.md) is described where its users look, or <run>/notes/<id>.md names why it needs no documentation.
    2. Every document changed in this stage was reread after its last edit, and each command or example it shows ran, or <run>/notes/<id>.md says why it cannot run here.
    3. The README was assessed: it changed, or <run>/notes/<id>.md says why it did not.
    4. No changed document copies a contract that has an authoritative home; it links to that home.
  Repeat while: Repeat while a changed public behaviour is undocumented or a reread or example run found a wrong statement; there is no iteration limit. Stop blocked only when a behaviour cannot be observed here (name it).
  Contract (written by ShipLoop; start from it unchanged): <run>/loops/<id>-contract.json
  Receipt: <run>/loops/<id>-terminal.json
How to invoke: on Claude Code, the Skill tool with skill "until-loop" and this argument; on any host, open the
card <abs until-loop ADAPTER.md> and follow it with this argument. Either way the loop starts with:
  python3 <abs until_loop_ephemeral.py> start --receipt <run>/loops/<id>-terminal.json < <run>/loops/<id>-contract.json
Never write or edit the receipt. After a reset, if the receipt exists and its status is active, run its next_argv once; do not start again.

Durable facts go in the repository's docs, never only in run notes. Do not document behaviour you did not observe as working.
Step plan paths: <paths>. ShipLoop commits, when verify is accepted, the declared paths, changed documentation files and docs/shiploop/; commit nothing yourself. <item_left(mode)>

DONE WHEN (the loop's exit conditions, the same words)
1. Every changed public behaviour (each public entry point, command, API, setting or screen in <run>/lint/<id>-inventory.md) is described where its users look, or <run>/notes/<id>.md names why it needs no documentation.
2. Every document changed in this stage was reread after its last edit, and each command or example it shows ran, or <run>/notes/<id>.md says why it cannot run here.
3. The README was assessed: it changed, or <run>/notes/<id>.md says why it did not.
4. No changed document copies a contract that has an authoritative home; it links to that home.
- evidence_refs lists the receipt <run>/loops/<id>-terminal.json.
Checked by: ShipLoop checks the terminal packet against the contract, then refuses a mechanical fault (no outcome or summary, an absolute evidence_refs path that does not exist, a credential pattern). ShipLoop issues this stage only when the item's changed paths include code (item_scope.behavioural); otherwise it records not applicable.
Outcomes: done | blocked | revise (the plan or a criterion is wrong as observed: name it).

RUN  the INVOKE block above · result template · callback · recovery · pause
FILES  grounding: spec, architecture.md, environment.md (absolute paths) · change inventory <run>/lint/<id>-inventory.md · results: step-plan, implement, test · run/reference.md#documentation, #current-system-baseline (only when this item recovered existing behaviour), #service-handoff (only when it selected a service)

contract.work: Run each changed public behaviour (from the change inventory) and update the README, API, operator and error documentation from what you observe, including the errors a user can see and how to turn on diagnostics; state known limits and caveats; link to the authoritative home instead of copying a contract; then reread every document you changed and run its commands and examples.
contract.exit_condition: (1) Every changed public behaviour (each public entry point, command, API, setting or screen in <run>/lint/<id>-inventory.md) is described where its users look, or <run>/notes/<id>.md names why it needs no documentation. (2) Every document changed in this stage was reread after its last edit, and each command or example it shows ran, or <run>/notes/<id>.md says why it cannot run here. (3) The README was assessed: it changed, or <run>/notes/<id>.md says why it did not. (4) No changed document copies a contract that has an authoritative home; it links to that home.
contract.repeat_condition: Repeat while a changed public behaviour is undocumented or a reread or example run found a wrong statement; there is no iteration limit. Stop blocked only when a behaviour cannot be observed here (name it).

stages.gate_after: quality-terminal-style check of <run>/loops/<id>-terminal.json against the contract (complete, exit satisfied) -> all four exits are the loop's assessment; exit 1: model evidence (script can only confirm notes/<id>.md exists or a docs-class path changed when the inventory has a public entry point); exit 2: model evidence; exit 3: script can check README.md changed or notes/<id>.md contains 'README'; exit 4: model evidence. For each completion criterion, name the passing command or the inspection that confirms it now (stale, skipped or missing evidence is not a confirmation); classify every test-spec case passed, failed, blocked or not due (with its phase and owner); a pass on another surface only supports. 3. From the change inventory, list every new or changed public entry point (exported function, CLI, request or event handler, callback); walk one valid, one boundary and one invalid input to its return, error or side effect, and write one trace line per path in <run>/notes/<id>.md; a wrong, unhandled or untested path is a finding (add a test for an untested path). 4. Review the whole item's diff against the step plan's steps and paths, the Code craft rubric and architecture.md: argument checks and contract docstrings at each entry point, missing error paths, silent failures, comments that restate or are stale, dead code, user text that is concatenated or bypasses the catalog, names outside the planned namespace or exported wider than needed, stored data off the planned schema, a near-copy of existing logic, a plain interaction where the plan called for a rich one, and a deviation from architecture.md with no new AD-<n>. 5. Chained or parallel work only: confirm the chain's finish commit is an ancestor of HEAD, inspect the combined diff, conflicts and the shared interfaces between steps. 6. Classify: material = wrong behaviour on a traced path, a missing or wrong argument check, contract, error path or test, a failing command, a misleading comment, logic that should have been composed; trivial = wording, ordering, a sharper name. Do not reopen a finding an earlier iteration fixed unless its code changed. 7. Fix every finding within scope by changing the work, never a check or its expected result; if anything changed, rerun step 1 and record the results.
  Exit when ALL of these hold (each shown by a command or file, after the last edit):
    1. Every recorded command (focused, regression, check) exited 0 in this iteration's run after the last edit, each running at least one test and every ID listed for it.

    5. Chained or parallel work only: git -C <worktree> merge-base --is-ancestor <chain finish commit> HEAD exits 0.
    6. Every later-phase check the criteria need (system, release, real boundary) is listed in <run>/notes/<id>.md with its owner and due stage.
    7. The latest complete iteration found no material finding.
  Repeat while: Repeat while the latest iteration fixed a material finding, a command failed, or a criterion or entry point is still unconfirmed; there is no iteration limit. Consult, and cite the headings you used:

- architecture.md (## Decisions, ## Superseded): the AD-<n> this item added or changed.
- environment.md (## Commands, ## Skills) and test-strategy.md (## Harnesses and suites).
